message_1:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha@fintechlabs.com>, Rajiv Kumar <rajiv@fintechlabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Fintech Labs cost & latency goals

Samantha / Rajiv — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and agreed next steps so nothing slips between meetings. I kept this tight.

Key pain points you shared
- Token/unit economics are the primary gating factor: expected 1M inference requests / week with high variance across batch jobs, current spend on inference is ~40% of ML infra budget.
- Latency sensitivity for end-user flows: p95 target ~200ms for typical 512-token summaries; bursty traffic during market open is a concern.
- Ops overhead: in-house serving pipeline (PyTorch-based, running on mixed g4/g5 fleet) has been hard to maintain at scale and teams want clearer TCO for moving to hosted/dedicated.

Current stack & constraints
- Models: proprietary fine-tuned LLaMA-family checkpoints (fp16), average output length 350–600 tokens, some requests hit 1024.
- Hosting: hybrid — primary on AWS (us-west-2), some on-prem for regulated datasets.
- Security/regulatory: data residency required for certain customer segments (US-only for payments data).

Success criteria (what would make a POC successful)
- Per-inference cost reduced by >=30% for the 512-token median case (or clear plan to reach this via batching + quantization).
- Maintain p95 latency <= 250ms (target 200ms) for core summary endpoint during normal load; have a defined graceful degradation path during market bursts.
- No data exfiltration risk; support for VPC/private deployment for regulated workload sample.

Technical openness we heard
- Quantization: your infra team is willing to trial int8; int4 is TBD but not ruled out.
- Batching/caching: open to prefix/KV caching and conservative batching windows (50–100ms) to avoid added tail latency.

Agreed next steps
1) Redwood: deliver a tailored 1-page TCO estimate + POC outline (what we’ll run, success metrics, telemetry we’ll collect). I will attach a draft POC outline and the prompt set we discussed. (attachment: redwood_poc_outline.pdf, fintech_prompt_set.csv)
2) Fintech Labs: share a short traffic snapshot and any regulatory checklist we must account for (attachment: fintech_traffic_snapshot.csv — if you can send this later today, we’ll fold into the TCO).
3) Tech deep-dive: schedule a 60-min session next week between Fintech infra, Vivek (SE), and our runtime folks to scope KV cache feasibility and quantization risk.
4) Contracting: high-level pricing bands in TCO; formal SOW/contract conversation after POC success metrics are agreed.

Tentative timeline
- POC start: target week of July 20 (2-week pilot) — flexible if you need more prep time.

If I missed anything important, flag it and I’ll update. I’ll follow up with the TCO + PoC outline by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

--

Samantha / team — quick technical clarifications so we scope the POC correctly:
1) Model family & tokenization: can you confirm the exact LLaMA variant + tokenizer version and whether sequences are commonly truncated or padded at 1024? This affects KV cache behavior.
2) Request distribution: do you have a % breakdown by seq-length buckets (0-128, 129-512, 513-1024)? If you cannot share raw logs, a histogram is fine.
3) Cold-starts vs warm requests: are you seeing large cold-start rates (e.g., traffic hitting many rarely-used user contexts) or is the workload concentrated on a smaller set of hot prefixes?
4) Quantization tolerance: for the evaluation set you’ll share, is there an automated metric we can run to quantify quality delta (ROUGE/BLEU/later human eval)? We’ll use that to recommend int8 vs int4.

For the POC we propose: a dedicated 2-week pilot where we run the 512-token summary endpoint through Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with prefix/KV caching enabled and a conservative 75ms batching window. We’ll collect per-token cost, p95 latency, and a prompt-level quality snapshot. If Fintech is comfortable, we can run parallel int8-inference jobs on a small portion of traffic to measure delta.

I’ll follow up with a short tech agenda for the deep-dive (KV caching feasibility, dataset redaction, quantization plan).

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
